While Axios itself does not directly create prototype pollution, if Object.prototype.transformResponse is already polluted by other vulnerabilities within the JavaScript process, affected versions of Axios may treat the inherited value as request configuration or option validators. Exploitation of this vulnerability requires a precondition: another prototype pollution vulnerability must exist or the attacker must have control over Object.prototype before Axios issues the request. Affected Versions Affected: Versions between 0.19.0 and 0.31.1 (exclusive), as well as versions prior to 1.15.2. Fixed Versions: 0.31.1 and 1.15.2. Details Vulnerability Type: Prototype Pollution Gadget. Trigger Mechanism: When Object.prototype.transformResponse is polluted, Axios may erroneously treat this inherited property as a legitimate request configuration item or validation option when parsing request configurations. Prerequisites for Exploitation: Axios is not the source of pollution. The attacker must first pollute Object.prototype or control its attributes through other vulnerabilities or methods within the same JavaScript process before triggering Axios's abnormal behavior. Impact If the exploitation prerequisites are met, an attacker can induce Axios to process unexpected configuration or validation logic.
